anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions compete for mutually incompatible locks, causing blocking chains or deadlocks in the lock-manager layer.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly : Commit processing is throttled by slow redo generation, flushing, or archiving in the write-ahead log subsystem.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes saturate host CPU capacity, leaving too few cycles for other work.

When all three root causes occur together the database experiences a compounded slowdown: commits are delayed by log-flush waits, so transactions hold locks longer, creating larger blocker–waiter trees and more frequent deadlocks. The enlarged lock queues in turn inflate session counts, context switches, and deadlock detection scans, which further consume CPU. Overall, users observe escalating commit latency, growing lock-wait and log-sync wait events, spikes in CPU run-queue length, widespread statement slow-downs, connection-pool exhaustion, and flurries of deadlock-victim or lock-timeout errors.

Causally, a saturated transaction-log path extends the duration of every commit, lengthening the time locks are held and sharply raising the probability of lock contention. The ensuing blocking and deadlock resolution workload drives additional CPU demand (lock-manager bookkeeping, deadlock graph construction, rollback processing). This extra CPU load competes with the log writer and archiver threads, slowing log flushes even more and creating a feedback loop that amplifies both the log bottleneck and lock contention. The mutually reinforcing pressures can push the system into a state where throughput collapses and recovery actions (forced rollbacks, failovers, or manual session kills) become necessary.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time with no network activity after which the operating system should send a TCP keepalive message to the client.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP client connection has no network activity longer than tcp_keepalives_idle on systems supporting TCP_KEEPIDLE or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Starts TCP keepalive probing for an otherwise idle client connection; together with interval and count settings this can lead to dead connection detection.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
